newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks first-quarter earnings up 50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks first-quarter earnings up 50 percent.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. posted a 50 percent increase in quarterly profits Thursday and announced plans to rapidly expand operations in Asia.

For the fiscal first quarter ending Dec. 29, the Seattle-based coffee bar chain reported net income of $14.4 million, or 18 cents a share, compared with $9.6 million, or 13 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.
Revenues rose 41 percent to $239.1 million from $169.5 million.
The earnings were in line with the Wall Street consensus of 18 cents a share, according to First Call. Starbucks stock rose $1.25 to close at $35 a share on Nasdaq.
Same-store sales rose only 3 percent in the quarter, but profit margins improved due to lower coffee costs, analysts said.
"It was a solid quarter in light of difficult holiday sales," said analyst Diane Daggatt of Dain Bosworth. She said bad weather and a disappointing assortment of non-coffee merchandise hurt results.
Starbucks also said it plans to have at least 200 Pacific Rim stores by the year 2000 in addition to the targeted 2,000 in North America.
Currently the company has 1,102 stores in North America plus five in the Pacific Rim markets of Hawaii, Tokyo and Singapore that were opened last year under licensing or joint-venture arrangements.
Starbucks also told analysts it had begun testing the sale of whole coffee beans in Portland, Ore., supermarkets and would expand the test to Austin, Texas.
"I think it opens up dramatic new possibilities if they can break into the supermarket channel," said analyst Hank Wilson of Hambrecht & Quist.
He said about $8 billion worth of coffee is sold in U.S. supermarkets annually and estimated that high-grade gourmet varieties could account for 10 percent of the total.
He said any decision on broad supermarket distribution probably would not come before 1998.

The supermarket test is just the latest in a series of initiatives to build on the growing brand-name recognition of Starbucks, which analysts compare to such well-known consumer brands as Coke and Nike.

Starbucks already is planning national distribution of its bottled Frappucino beverage in a venture with Pepsico Inc. and it sells Starbucks premium ice cream in a venture with Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream Inc..
Starbucks also said Thursday it would open stores in the Miami and Detroit markets this year.
